entry.name: Clinician Bathing Demonstrations
entry.title: High Fidelity Capture, Reconstruction, and Transfer of Human Demonstrations for Robot-Assisted Bathing
entry.summary: Three trained clinicians wiping the arms, legs, thighs, obliques, back, neck and face of six seated subjects with wet wipes, wearing a 65-taxel capacitive Pressure Profile Systems TactileGlove on each hand (10 Hz) inside a 20-camera Vicon capture at 120 Hz; 128 captures, 257,000 frames, with SMPL-X and MANO fits, contact regions and force.
entry.hand: Pressure Profile Systems TactileGlove on both hands of the clinician

sensor.note: 65 differential-capacitance pressure taxels per glove across the palm and digits, synchronised with Vicon by timecode; 3M TB641 grip material added to the glove palms.

scale.text: 128 captures, 257,000 frames (mean 2,007 frames per capture), 3 clinicians bathing 6 subjects, 8 body regions

entry.access: The paper says 'All relevant materials will be publicly released'; no dataset link or repository was given (checked 2026-11-24).
caveats: The touch is human-on-human contact through a wet wipe during bathing, not object manipulation on a table.
No RGB video of the demonstrations is described; capture is Vicon markers (52 on each subject, 23 on the back of each glove) plus the gloves.
The paper reports 128 captures, while its per-region table sums to 138.
Hands, chest and pelvis of the subjects were not bathed in the captures.

tracking.note: 23 markers on the back of each glove; MANO fitted from markers
52 markers on each person; SMPL-X fitted with MoSh++

sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09127 (abstract via arXiv API; v1, 2026-08-10, RSS 2026)
https://arxiv.org/html/2608.09127 (capture setup, gloves, scale, release sentence)
unconfirmed: subjects 9 counts 3 clinicians and 6 bathed subjects; only the clinicians wore the gloves.
The paper cites the glove as Pressure Profile Systems 'TactileGlove' without a revision; the 65-taxel count matches the catalog's TactileGlove II record.
Coverage tip, phalanx and palm is from the paper's 'across the palm and digits'; the exact element layout was not read.
hours not stated; 257,000 frames at the 120 Hz Vicon rate would be about 0.6 h, which assumes frames are counted at that rate.
